subject: [PATCH v3 08/12] mm/collapse: separate scanning a PTE table from collapsing it

2026-09-16.patch_summary: This patch separates the scanning of a PTE table from its collapse into two distinct functions: `collapse_scan_pmd` and `collapse_run_pmd`. The scan function reads the PTE table under the mmap_lock, while the run function performs the actual collapse. This change improves code organization and reduces the complexity of the original `collapse_single_pmd` function.

2026-09-18.patch_summary: This patch separates the scanning of a PTE table from its collapse into two distinct functions: `collapse_scan_pmd` and `collapse_run_pmd`. The scan function reads the table under the mmap_lock, while the run function performs the actual collapse. This change improves code organization and reduces the complexity of the original `collapse_single_pmd` function. Additionally, it allows for more efficient handling of file tables by khugepaged and introduces changes to tracing events.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David (Arm) noted that the naming of functions in the patch is suboptimal and inconsistent, suggesting renaming collapse_single_pmd() to collapse_pmd(), and then renaming collapse_scan_pmd() and collapse_run_pmd() to collapse_scanned_pmd() and collapse_scan_pmd() respectively.

Reviewer David (Arm) questioned whether adding more locking to the file path was intended, and asked for clarification on what 'only reads' means in the context of collapse_scan_file()

Reviewer David (Arm) suggested breaking up the patch into separate patches, citing that the changes are 'squeezed' into the last part of the description and are difficult to understand when presented together.

Reviewer David noted that the use of _put functions without putting anything, marked as BUG, is awkward and requested a reevaluation

Reviewer David (Arm) expressed concern that the introduction of collapse_control_release() is unnecessary and could be simplified, suggesting a minimal interface for the collapse function
reviews.raw_body:
Makes sense.

The naming is a bit suboptimal and inconsistent.

collapse_single_pmd
-> collapse_scan_pmd()
-> collapse_run_pmd()

Maybe it would be clearer:

collapse_pmd() ["single" is rather useless]
-> collapse_scan_pmd()
-> collapse_scanned_pmd()

---

So we add more locking to the file path to merge both paths cleanly? Or did I
misunderstand that paragraph?

What do you mean with "and only reads"?

---

Is there any way we could move these changes into separate patches? These
changes are bit squeezed into the last part of this description. And having to
much happening at once makes this rather hard to grasp.

---

See below regarding _release: having _put functions that are not supposed to put
anything except with BUG is akward.

---

Do we really have to introduce collapse_control_release() just to perform some
safety checks for BUGs? I'd rather keep the collapse interface minimal and not
introduce _release semantics when there is actually nothing to be released?

Or will you add more into _release in later patches in this series?


-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that the naming of functions is awkward and explained their reasoning for using 'scan' and 'run' prefixes, indicating a design choice rather than an error.

The author addressed David's concern that the mmap_lock is dropped before the file scan, explaining that this results in unnecessary lock drops and relocks for most scans. The author plans to mirror the anonymous side by dropping the lock only after a scan finds work.

Author clarified that the scan function only determines if there is work to be done, and the collapse function (collapse_file()) performs the actual collapse; author agreed to remove unnecessary wording.

Author acknowledged that the patch had a performance issue where every file table, even refused ones, caused an unnecessary unlock, relock, and VMA lookup. They plan to rewrite the code to fix this.

Author addressed David's concern about a potential issue in the patch series, specifically the engine that gives both jobs, by stating it will be dropped from this series and added separately with the engine posted.
reviews.raw_body:
Yes, the naming is awkward.

The problem is that collapse_ is the prefix of everything in the
interface, so it cannot double as the verb: collapse_pmd() says what the
function is about, not what it does, and collapse_scanned_pmd() has no
verb at all.

Each name needs one after the prefix, hence scan and run. I don't
particularly like it, but it seems better than scan and scanned, no?

collapse_single_pmd() itself goes away in the next patch. You asked
there why; I will answer there.

---

The lock is held over the scan now, but it is taken fewer times. The
current code drops mmap_lock before the file scan, before it knows if
there is anything to collapse. Most scans find nothing, and each of them
pays the cost of unlock and relock for nothing.

Dropping the lock only after a scan found work mirrors the anonymous
side, with the same batching shape.

---

That it no longer calls collapse_file(). The scan looks at the page
cache and says whether there is work; collapse_file() is the run's job.

I will drop the wording. It does not help.

---

It is also wrong, so I will rewrite it.

Before this patch collapse_single_pmd() set lock_dropped for every file
table, refused or not, and collapse_scan_mm_slot() bailed out on it.

The mm slot stays, so the next call comes back to the same mm at the
saved address, but every file table cost an unlock, a trip through
khugepaged_do_scan(), a relock and a VMA lookup.

Now only a table that gets collapsed pays that.

---

Not in this series.

The engine I have on top of it gives both a job.

I will drop it from this series and add it with the engine. The shape
might change by the time the engine is posted.

The check at the top of collapse_scan_pmd() stays, open-coded: a scan
that found work on a file table holds a reference, and the next scan is
where one that was never run gets caught.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov
